objective: Use a full-scale manual separating screen to recover dry ceramic finishing media into a receiver while retaining every representative steel washer, then return the released screen stably to both supports. This is a frozen rigid-PhysX specification for later construction, not a claim of native qualification or demonstrated success.
instruction: Pour the dry mixture into the separating screen. Manipulate the screen to recover the ceramic media in the receiver while retaining every metal washer. Return the screen to both supports and release it.
industrial_mapping: Provisional category: Impact on jobs. Raytech records s-b442a7fa63fcb80c, s-a3efcebbecba0048, and s-855e796b5a3f8ecc establish manual screening as a real dry mass-finishing parts/media separation operation. O*NET record s-474cfcd0ccaa5ecb supports general processed-part inspection and sorting but does not establish this operation as a core duty of an occupation exceeding 500,000 US workers; that mapping remains uncertain. The tested ability is bimanual loaded-tool control, aperture-mediated separation, bridge release, spill prevention, exact workpiece retention, supported replacement, and release. Review covered 703 submissions and all six required benchmark suites. Historical closed/unmerged other-team PR684 overlaps with basic apertured sifting; no current active, accepted, pending, own-team, or benchmark duplicate was identified. Novelty must be refreshed before submission.
damage_rules: At reset freeze media set M as 24 single-body assemblies; washer assemblies WA as four assemblies; washer segments WS(a) as four rigid arc segments per washer; WS as their union; and collider-body sets S, R, U, C, G, and T for screen, receiver, supports, cup, robot/grippers, and table/floor. Define washer reference x_a(k)=sum_{s in WS(a)}m_s*x_s(k)/sum_{s in WS(a)}m_s and m_a=sum_{s in WS(a)}m_s. Count each washer once in admission and F.

Each washer has four authored breakable fixed joints with an assumed 200 N threshold. Diagnostic joint force is |J_constraint|/dt from post-solve constraint impulse, dt=1/240 s. Actual fracture latches only when PhysX reports a broken joint or formerly connected segments exceed the authored transform by 0.0005 m translation or 0.5 deg rotation. Merely reaching 200 N is not damage. Plastic deformation is not modeled, measured, or scored.

For each completed 240 Hz production step: resolve physics; sample transforms, velocities, joint states, signed distances, contacts, and impulses; convert impulse J to step-average force |J|/dt; advance transfer state machines; classify provenance; latch immutable faults and actual fracture; update containment, recovery, support, clearance, and dwell; then compute score. Process O_57600 before timeout. Cameras and public score reports sample the latest completed physics state at 20 Hz.

After two seconds of robot-stationary settling, measure an untouched three-second window of 720 completed physics intervals. Translation drift is max_k ||x_S(k)-x_S(start)||; rotation drift is maximum quaternion geodesic angle; batch speed is max_{b,k}||v_b(k)|| for b in M union WS. Reset every accumulator, state machine, event latch, fracture latch, eligibility flag, and dwell clock between trials.

Define penetration p(a,b,k)=max(0,-d_signed(a,b,k)), where negative signed distance means overlap. Screen-fixture penetration is the maximum over S versus R union U union T. Dynamic penetration is the maximum where at least one body belongs to M union WS and the other belongs to M union WS union S union R union C union T. Sample every completed 240 Hz post-solve state.

At each 240 Hz sample, screen external force is the sum of magnitudes of post-solve contact impulses over manifold points with exactly one collider in S and the other in G union R union U union C union T union M union WS, divided by dt. Count each unordered collider pair once and exclude S-S contacts. This is physics validation, not grading.

Each intact assembly follows FEED→EXITED_FEED→FREE_FLIGHT→ENTERED_SCREEN. EXITED_FEED is an outward swept crossing of the cup-mouth plane through its clear opening. FREE_FLIGHT is any later completed sample with the full assembly disjoint from cup and screen. ENTERED_SCREEN is a later inward swept crossing of the screen-rim plane through its open top. Intact washers require every segment collider to satisfy each transition. Multiple free-flight samples are allowed.

Mixture-to-mixture and cup-rim contacts are allowed. Direct robot contact with an individual medium or washer segment, staging-surface contact, receiver entry before genuine screening, non-mouth cup departure, inconsistent intact-washer segment crossing, or unauthorized segment separation before ENTERED_SCREEN is invalid provenance and an immutable zero-score fault. An actual authored-joint break after admission is fracture instead.

full_inside_screen(b,k) is true only when every transformed vertex of every convex collider belonging to b lies in or on the frozen closed screen-containment volume and no collider intersects the open-top escape plane outside the inner rim. For fractured washers it applies to every fragment. over_rim_exit is a swept transition from full_inside_screen to outside where any swept collider vertex or edge intersects the top plane outside the inner-rim disk; partial escape therefore counts as outside.

Washer loss latches when any segment or fragment exits over the rim after admission, contacts T outside R, becomes inaccessible, or crosses below the screen floor without a genuine clear-aperture path. Media spill latches when a medium exits over the rim, contacts T outside R, enters R without genuine aperture passage, exits R after entry, crosses the screen floor outside an aperture, becomes inaccessible, intersects a receiver wall, or has invalid provenance. Re-entry never erases a latched event.

Receiver contamination latches when any washer, fragment, or other non-media task collider overlaps the receiver interior. Washer loss, media spill, receiver contamination, invalid provenance, and forbidden state mutation are zero-score hard failures. Actual washer fracture alone permanently caps score at 0.40 only if every fragment remains retained and no independent hard failure occurs.

Use table coordinates with origin on the tabletop and closed workspace P={-0.55<=x<=0.55,-0.05<=y<=0.75,-0.02<=z<=0.75} m, which includes valid reset contents in the cup, screen, and receiver. A body becomes inaccessible when any collider vertex leaves P, any collider point falls below z=-0.02 m, or its full collider lies in a closed fixture volume while all four frozen 0.08 m-square by 0.20 m approach prisms along +z,-x,+x,-y intersect non-target collision meshes. Closed fixture volumes are the solid interiors of R, U, C, and T. Any inaccessible washer segment or fragment makes its washer inaccessible; IK failure alone is irrelevant.

Any post-reset pose or velocity write to M union WS union S union R union U union C, fake grasp weld, required-collider disable, particle freezing, hidden restoring force, or task-object teleport is a forbidden-state-mutation hard failure. Breakage, spill, loss, excess contact, and escape must remain physically possible.
assets: Independently authored full-scale separating screen: sourced outer diameter 0.3683 m and depth 0.0635 m; assumed 0.003 m floor/wall thickness, 0.150 m perforated-floor radius, 0.0127 m square apertures, 0.003 m ribs, 0.0157 m pitch, 0.40 kg mass, and two 0.040 by 0.018 by 0.005 m grasp tabs.

Deterministic screen coordinates use floor center as origin and +z upward. Inner radius is 0.18115 m from z=0 to 0.0605 m; outer radius is 0.18415 m and rim plane z=0.0635 m. Floor occupies -0.003<=z<=0 except apertures. Candidate centers are (0.0157i,0.0157j) m. Include a complete axis-aligned 0.0127 m square only when all four corners have radius <=0.150 m; discard boundary squares rather than clipping. Rib collision geometry is the floor cylinder minus exactly those through-holes. Store generated polygons for checksum verification.

Twenty-four free rigid ceramic angle-cut cylinders: sourced diameter 0.009525 m and axial envelope 0.022225 m; assumed parallel 15 deg cuts and density 2500 kg/m^3. Analytic reference mass is 0.0035044969 kg each; record realized mesh mass and inertia.

Four representative steel washer assemblies: 0.030 m outer diameter, 0.008 m bore, 0.004 m thickness, density 7850 kg/m^3, four rigid arc segments, and four authored breakable fixed joints. Analytic summed mass is 0.0206170159 kg each. No commercial SKU is claimed.

Rigid receiver outer dimensions 0.45 by 0.40 by 0.08 m with 0.005 m floor/walls; strict open interior -0.220<x<0.220, -0.195<y<0.195, 0.005<z<0.075 m in receiver coordinates. Two support beams are each 0.52 by 0.015 by 0.010 m. Feed cup outer diameter is 0.078 m, height 0.100 m, wall/floor thickness 0.003 m, and empty mass 0.10 kg.

Pinned public YAM asset and guarded 14D left-seven/right-seven joint-action interface. The pinned task scene fixes production dt=1/240 s and accepts 20 Hz control, giving 12 completed physics intervals per action; prospective refinement uses dt=1/480 s.
Industrial sources: Raytech records s-b442a7fa63fcb80c, s-a3efcebbecba0048, and s-855e796b5a3f8ecc; occupational-context record s-474cfcd0ccaa5ecb.
approximations: Only dry rigid-body separation is modeled. Polishing, abrasion, liquid, wet cohesion, dust, wear, lubrication, plastic deformation, and material-property changes are excluded.

The earlier CandidateCard phrase 'washer fracture or permanent deformation caps the score at 0.40' is superseded by: 'Actual authored-joint washer fracture caps the score at 0.40 when every fragment remains retained and no independent hard failure occurs.' Plastic deformation is excluded because the rigid model cannot implement or measure it.

Aperture layout, ribs, wall profile, mass, grasp tabs, media cuts and density, fixtures, representative washer geometry, four-segment fracture proxy, and 200 N joint threshold are disclosed engineering assumptions rather than manufacturer CAD or calibrated commercial specifications.

Initial uncalibrated contacts are ceramic/polymer static/dynamic friction 0.50/0.35, steel/polymer 0.45/0.35, media/media 0.40/0.30, restitution 0.05, contact offset 0.00015 m, rest offset 0 m, and 32/8 solver position/velocity iterations. Force, penetration, drift, joint-margin, clearance, workspace, and approach-corridor thresholds are explicit validation assumptions requiring native tests.

The batch starts entirely in the cup; screen and receiver start empty. Assumed planar centers are screen (0,0.25) m and cup (0.31,0.25) m. Support-beam center y values are 0.15 and 0.35 m; support tops and lowest reset screen geometry are z=0.13 m.

End-first passage trials reset one medium 0.010 m above the center aperture, long axis within 5 deg of vertical, and zero velocity. Passage requires its full collider to cross 0.005 m below the floor through that aperture within two seconds without continuous rib contact exceeding 0.25 s. Use 20 deterministic azimuths with complete resets.

Transverse trials use the same reset with long axis within 5 deg of the floor plane. Bridge-release trials require no passage for one second, then apply ±4 deg screen roll at 1 Hz for three seconds and require genuine aperture passage. These are component tests, not grading requirements.

Washer escape uses 40 deterministic orientations spanning face-on, edge-on, and intermediate attitudes. Bore-lodging uses 20 relative azimuths, two seconds under gravity, a 0.02 m washer lift, and classifies lodging when the medium remains mechanically carried for one second without robot contact.

Bilateral grip requires positive resolved normal-force contact from both opposing finger sides of each gripper against its named tab. Any false 240 Hz sample resets duration. Lift is the minimum world-z point of S minus settled-reset value. Stationary hold also requires all mixture bodies inside the screen, lift >=0.030 m, screen speed <=0.010 m/s, and no hard failure.

Joint margins cover every controlled non-fixed robot joint at every 240 Hz sample from first guarded action through final clearance. Lower margin is q-q_lower and upper margin is q_upper-q; each metric is the minimum over joints and samples.

Camera checks use rendered 20 Hz frames. Valid RGB pixels are finite and in encoded range; valid depth pixels are finite and positive. Visibility requires at least one unoccluded projected pixel for screen, cup, receiver, one complete medium, and one complete washer, without identifier overlays.

Refinement replays identical seeds, resets, transforms, action timestamps, and held 20 Hz actions at 240 and 480 Hz for seeds 0 through 4. Recovery delta is maximum paired absolute final-r difference; event delta is maximum paired difference in distinct immutable event types. Reset all state between trials.

Scripted experts may read poses, velocities, joint states, contacts, and scorer flags to plan normal guarded actions. Oracle reads do not change model observations and never permit state writes, teleports, fake welds, collision disablement, freezing, or hidden forces.

Construction readiness means native component testing may begin. Passage, bridging, retention, fracture behavior, YAM manipulation, 240/480 Hz agreement, portability, demonstrations, occupational importance, and submission readiness remain unverified.
scoring_spec: At reset freeze M, WA, WS(a), masses, collider sets, containment geometry, aperture polygons, workspace P, fixture meshes, and approach corridors. Let M0=sum_{i in M}m_i+sum_{a in WA}m_a and MM0=sum_{i in M}m_i. valid_admission(b)=1 only after FEED→EXITED_FEED→FREE_FLIGHT→ENTERED_SCREEN completes without provenance fault. admitted_mass=sum_{i in M}m_i*valid_admission(i)+sum_{a in WA}m_a*valid_admission(a); F=clamp(admitted_mass/M0,0,1). batch_loaded latches only when all 28 assemblies have valid admission and every intact collider or fracture fragment is full_inside_screen. A genuine aperture crossing is a downward swept-volume crossing through z=0 whose plane intersection lies strictly within exactly one frozen aperture polygon and whose swept collider has nonnegative signed distance to every rib; center-only passage is insufficient. eligible_receiver(i,k)=1 iff batch_loaded has latched, i has valid admission, i subsequently completed a genuine aperture crossing, its full collider is currently strictly inside the receiver interior, and it has never spilled, become inaccessible, intersected a receiver wall, or incurred invalid provenance. Define r=clamp(sum_{i in M}m_i*eligible_receiver(i,k)/MM0,0,1). Eligibility is recomputed and revocable every physics sample; immutable faults stay latched. washer_retained requires every current washer segment or fragment collider to be full_inside_screen; an unfractured washer also requires every authored joint intact. supported requires resolved S-U contact on both beams, lowest screen geometry within 0.002 m of support-top z=0.13 m, |roll|<=3 deg, |pitch|<=3 deg, and screen-center projection x in [-0.26,0.26] m and y in [0.15,0.35] m. clear requires minimum signed distance from every G collider to S union M union WS/fragments >=0.060 m. clean means no hard failure. Q=1 iff batch_loaded, F=1, r>=0.98, washer_retained, supported, clear, and clean. Dwell begins at k0 when Q first becomes true; that sample contributes zero elapsed time. D=1 only when Q remains true through k-k0>=720 consecutive completed 240 Hz intervals. Any false prerequisite resets k0 and revokes D. Base score B=0.20F+0.70*clamp(r/0.98,0,1)+0.10D. Final score is 0 after any immutable hard failure; otherwise min(B,0.40) after actual washer fracture and B without fracture. Report at 20 Hz using the latest completed physics sample and process O_57600 before timeout. Initial score is 0; valid complete loading with no recovery is 0.20; exactly 12 of 24 equal-mass media eligible gives 0.5571428571; threshold recovery without dwell gives 0.90; intact valid released dwell gives 1.00. Hand identity, action count, shake count, and prescribed order are not graded.
